title: Chapter 78: I Can't Control My Right Hand
html:
Shall I go in to take a closer look?

Curiosity gnawed at Chen Ge. Mallet in hand, he desperately wanted to break down the door and see what was written on the paper.

According to the school forum, five students once broke into Mu Yang High School on a dare and played the Pen Spirit game in the last classroom. Did they leave the pen and paper behind?After a moment’s thought, he dismissed the idea. The post claimed that when two extra people appeared, the five students fled in panic. They must have knocked over some furniture in their escape, yet every desk and chair now stood in perfect order.

Of course, someone could have rearranged the furniture after they left. Or all five students could have been possessed.

Chen Ge lowered his mallet and decided to save the classroom for last. He left the education block and headed for the dormitory.

The squat, dilapidated building held only a handful of rooms. After circling it for some time, he found a faded iron sign. Its characters were smudged, but he believed it had once read: ‘Second Floor: Female Dormitory. No Male Admittance.’

This school sure is shabby.

Chen Ge removed his raincoat and dabbed at the water that had seeped beneath his collar. He was about to continue when his phone rang. He checked the caller ID and answered. “He San?”

“Boss, I’ve given my senior your phone number. She said that she would have her father contact you when he’s home.”

“Thanks. Anything else?”

“Also, Qin Guang just started his livestream. Are you sure you don’t want to look? He hired an actor to play the killer next door, and both his opening and his analysis are complete copies of yours. I don’t even know where to begin complaining.”

“Let him. But I’m starting my own stream soon, so remember to come support me.”

“You’re going live?!” He San’s voice shot up several octaves. Chen Ge was glad to have such a loyal viewer. “It’s been a while since my last stream, so I’ve planned something exciting tonight.”

The line went silent. Several seconds later came the slap of hurried footsteps. He San had evidently thrown on his slippers and begun racing around the bedroom, shaking every roommate awake. “Get up! It’s livestream time! Another dance with death tonight!”

Chen Ge appreciated the free promotion, though He San’s choice of words left him uneasy.

After hanging up, Chen Ge opened the video-sharing app. Qin Guang’s supernatural livestream was heavily promoted on the front page, so he clicked in for a quick look. A full production team was clearly behind it. A professional cameraman handled the filming, leaving Qin Guang free to analyze the scene and hunt for clues. The difference in video quality alone crushed Chen Ge’s stream. He could hardly fault his rival for being better prepared.

680,000 views. If I had that many views to promote my Haunted House, wouldn’t the whole park be filled the next day?

Livestreams and short videos were Chen Ge’s only means of advertising, and Qin Guang’s featured stream showed him a path forward. If he ever became that popular, perhaps the platform would devote the same resources to promoting him.

Don’t get ahead of yourself, Chen Ge. Focus on surviving tonight.

He left Qin Guang’s livestream and started his own. Out in the countryside, his connection was weak. The video blurred, lagged, and repeatedly cut to black; he could not even see the chat.

My video quality might not be as good as Qin Guang’s, but my content is definitely better than his…

Unable to see the chat, Chen Ge could not interact with his viewers. After briefly introducing Mu Yang High School, he stopped monitoring the stream. His search of the dormitory’s first floor turned up nothing, so he moved upstairs.

“The girls’ rooms look just like the boys’.”

Textbooks and garbage filled the rooms; most of the school’s contents had never been cleared away. Chen Ge searched each room patiently by flashlight. In the fourth room on the second floor, four chairs stood neatly in a row. Several sheets of white paper and a ballpoint pen rested on one of them.

“The paper and pen look brand new, so they must have been placed inside the room after the school was closed.”

This was the second time Chen Ge had found paper and pen arranged together. The rusted lock was little more than decoration; after he rattled it a few times, it fell away.

As the door opened, a wave of moldy air struck him. Covering his mouth and nose, Chen Ge approached the chair and examined the sheets of paper.

There were four sheets in total. The first read, ‘When will I die?’

The second read, ‘How will I die?’

The third read, ‘Who will be the next to die?’

The fourth was completely empty.

The Pen Spirit game?

Chen Ge searched the rest of the room for more clues, but time had reduced most of its contents to rot.

When the search yielded nothing, Chen Ge turned his attention back to the white paper. No one can fully explain the Pen Spirit game, but scientists say breathing, heartbeat, and blood flow cause tiny involuntary movements. An untrained person’s arm will naturally shift after being held aloft in one position for too long. It’s a bodily reaction, nothing to do with the Pen Spirit legend.

Chen Ge placed his phone on the bed, making sure both he and the four chairs were in frame.

Since I need to complete all four side missions at Mu Yang High School, might as well start with this one.

He closed the bedroom door, then stood hesitating for four full minutes before sitting and picking up the ballpoint pen.

He told himself not to worry. With the doll tucked into his chest pocket, the pen in his right hand, and the mallet in his left, he began the Pen Spirit game.

He recalled every detail he could from the thread. Raising his arm slightly, he held the pen upright with its tip against the white paper, closed his eyes, and chanted.

“Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, you are my spirit from my previous life, and I am your spirit in this life. If you are with us, please draw a circle on the paper.”

When the chant ended, Chen Ge forced himself to relax. His arm remained suspended over the paper, the rest of his body motionless.

Rain drummed beyond the window. Swallowed by night, the school began to change almost imperceptibly.

The room’s moldy odor faded. A cold draft from nowhere lifted the paper on the chair. Then Chen Ge’s eyes flew open—someone had gripped his hand.

Chen Ge stared closely at his right hand while his left hand tightened over the mallet. He would strike the moment things went wrong.
